title: Black Friday Facebook ads: how to choose products to push
summary: Not every product deserves your Black Friday budget. Learn how to find the SKUs worth pushing in Facebook catalog ads and keep spend off the rest.
body_markdown:
Every November, the same thing happens on Facebook and Instagram. More brands advertise, costs climb, and nearly everyone runs catalog ads at once. Then Meta's delivery system does what it was built to do: it finds the products that are easiest to sell and puts your budget behind them.


Those aren't always the products you need to sell. Some are low-margin. Some are about to run out. Meanwhile, your best opportunities can sit in the catalog with barely an impression.


This guide shows how to decide which products deserve your advertising investment through Black Friday and the weeks around it, and how to make Meta's catalog ads reflect those priorities. It covers when to get ready, how to find the products worth pushing, how to put those priorities into Meta, how to handle budget, audiences and creative, and what to change as the season moves on.


## When should you start Black Friday Facebook ads?


Black Friday falls on 27 November this year and Cyber Monday on 30 November, but peak season runs much longer than one weekend. Shopping and promotions build from the start of November and carry on to Christmas, with November doing most of the work. Most advertisers plan for the whole month, so the real deadline is the start of November.


Meta says ad review is typically completed within 24 hours, though it can take longer. New ad sets then go through a learning phase, which Meta says usually ends after about 50 results in the week following the last significant edit. Pausing an ad set or changing its audience, creative or optimization event counts as a significant edit, and large budget or bid changes can too.


So have your product priorities, catalog data, creative and campaign structure ready before November begins. That leaves time for review and learning, and lets you spend the month adjusting what you promote instead of rebuilding campaigns. Product decisions come first, because they shape everything else. If November has already started, begin there: your product priorities decide where the rest of the month's budget goes.


## Why does product selection matter so much on Meta?


Meta's automation now decides who sees your ad, where it runs, how much to bid and, in catalog ads, which product to show. The fewer controls you have over delivery, the more your choice of eligible products matters.


Left to itself, a full-catalog campaign tends to drift. A small share of products takes most of the spend. Strong products get too little. Products that are close to selling out keep getting pushed. And the campaign can still hit its targets, or get close to them, but it won't show you which products are driving its success and which are wasting your spend.


Cantão, a Brazilian fashion retailer with more than 4,000 products, saw exactly this in its Meta campaigns. An audit found a large share of spend going to products with low or zero conversions, while high-potential products were starved of impressions. In a five-week A/B test with identical spend, prioritizing the right products lifted ROAS by 24%, revenue by 24% and conversion rate by 12%. ([Read the Cantão case study](https://www.roihunter.com/success-stories/cant%C3%A3o-grows-roas-by-24-with-segment-prioritisation) )


The fix starts before the campaign does: decide which products deserve investment this season.


## How to identify which products deserve more advertising investment


Not every product in your catalog has the same revenue potential, and Meta doesn't have the full picture of your business.


Meta's algorithm optimizes delivery based on the signals available to it, but it doesn't automatically account for your product margins, inventory priorities, returns, or sales performance outside its platform. As a result, products receiving the most advertising exposure aren't necessarily the ones that will generate the greatest value for your business.


Before deciding which products to prioritize for Black Friday, look beyond Meta's reporting. Combine advertising performance with SKU-level sales data, conversion rates, margins, inventory availability, and performance across other channels.


This is particularly important for underpromoted products. A product receiving little advertising exposure on Meta may appear to have limited potential, even if it's generating strong sales on your website or through other channels.


Pattern Ad Signals (formerly ROI Hunter) brings these signals together to help retailers understand the performance and potential of individual SKUs. Its AI-driven SMART Segments continuously evaluate product performance to identify Top Performers, Poor Performers, and opportunities that might otherwise be overlooked.


Inventory availability adds another layer to your product strategy. Products with strong demand but limited stock may require a different approach from those with healthy inventory levels. For fashion retailers, size and color availability should also influence prioritization, especially during peak shopping periods.


New arrivals deserve special consideration. Without sufficient advertising history, they can struggle to receive meaningful exposure. Looking at early website sales, engagement, and cross-channel performance can help identify promising products before they accumulate enough Meta conversion data.


Using these signals, retailers can organize their Black Friday product strategy around four practical priorities:


### Push: high potential, enough stock


These are the products with strong revenue potential and sufficient inventory to support increased demand. They might include proven bestsellers, high-margin products, strong converters, or products showing promising performance outside Meta.


The goal: Increase their visibility in catalog ads and give Meta stronger signals about which products deserve more advertising investment.


Prioritize these SKUs for your Black Friday advertising strategy and support them with high-quality creatives, compelling promotional offers, and relevant placements across Facebook and Instagram.


With Pattern Ad Signals' Segment Prioritisation, retailers can influence Meta's product delivery toward these higher-priority products without having to isolate them in separate campaigns or product sets.


### Protect: high potential, stock at risk


Some of your strongest products may also be the most vulnerable to selling out during Black Friday.


A bestseller with limited inventory or an incomplete size range might generate excellent advertising returns, but aggressively increasing its exposure could lead to stockouts and missed sales opportunities.


The goal: Balance advertising exposure with inventory availability.


Monitor stock levels closely and adjust product priorities as availability changes. Where necessary, reduce promotional emphasis on products with limited supply and redirect attention toward relevant alternatives with healthier stock levels.


### Maintain: lower current potential, enough stock


Not every product needs to be a Black Friday bestseller to deserve advertising exposure.


Some products have healthy inventory but haven't yet demonstrated strong advertising performance. Others may be new arrivals, seasonal products, or products that perform well through channels outside Meta.


The goal: Maintain opportunities for discovery without disproportionately investing in products with weaker performance signals.


Rather than automatically excluding these products, keep them eligible where appropriate and continuously evaluate whether their performance justifies greater prioritization.


This is where cross-channel insights become especially valuable. Products that Meta hasn't promoted heavily may still have untapped revenue potential worth exploring.


### Pull: lower potential, limited stock or poor performance


Some products simply don't justify additional advertising investment during Black Friday.


These may include products consistently generating spend without sufficient conversions, products with weak profitability, or products with limited availability and little remaining revenue potential.


The goal: Reduce wasted advertising spend and create more opportunities for stronger-performing products.


Deprioritize products with consistently weak performance, while distinguishing poor performers from products that haven't received enough exposure to demonstrate their potential.


AI-driven segmentation makes this process easier to keep current by continuously reevaluating product performance instead of relying on manually maintained rules.


For example, Brazilian menswear retailer Reserva tested Pattern Ad Signals' SMART Segments against its existing manual segmentation strategy in Meta campaigns.


With identical budgets, targeting, creatives, and optimization settings, the AI-driven segmentation approach reduced spend on Poor Performers by 75%, increased ROAS by 17%, improved click-through rate by 17%, and reduced cost per click by 8%.


The results demonstrated how smarter, continuously updated product segmentation can improve advertising performance without increasing the overall budget.

## How do you activate your product priorities in Meta?


Identifying which products deserve more or less advertising exposure is only the first step. The next challenge is translating those priorities into your Meta catalog ads.


Traditionally, advertisers have relied on product sets to control which products are eligible for advertising. For example, you might build separate sets for bestsellers, new arrivals, discounted products, or low-stock items.


While this approach can work, creating too many separate product sets and campaigns introduces additional complexity. It can also fragment campaign learning, restrict the range of products available to Meta's algorithm, and require continuous manual adjustments as product performance changes.


There are two main ways to put a product prioritization strategy into action:


### Option 1: Manual segmentation with Meta product sets


If you're managing product priorities directly in Meta, you can organize your catalog using product attributes and labels.


- Define your product groups: Use available catalog data, product performance, margins, and stock information to determine which products should receive more or less exposure.
- Create product sets where necessary: Use product-set filters to include or exclude products from specific advertising activities. Meta's catalog has an internal label field built for this, which you can update as often as you need without sending products back through policy review.
- Keep your data updated: Refresh product classifications and inventory information regularly so your campaigns reflect changing business priorities.
- Avoid unnecessary fragmentation: Consolidate product sets and campaigns where possible to preserve Meta's ability to optimize across a broad selection of products.


The biggest limitation of this approach is maintenance. During Black Friday, product performance and inventory availability can change quickly, making manually managed segmentation difficult to keep current.


### Option 2: AI-driven segmentation and Segment Prioritisation with Pattern Ad Signals


Pattern Ad Signals provides a more automated approach to identifying and prioritizing products in Meta catalog campaigns.


SMART Segments continuously evaluate SKU-level performance using signals from advertising platforms, shopper behavior, and product data. Instead of relying on static rules, they automatically identify products with stronger performance potential and those consuming advertising spend inefficiently.


Segment Prioritisation takes this a step further by helping retailers influence which products Meta promotes within a broader catalog setup.


Rather than creating separate campaigns or product sets for every business priority, advertisers can prioritize stronger-performing SKUs and reduce exposure for weaker ones while maintaining a broad product selection available to Meta's delivery system.


This helps retailers balance two important objectives: giving Meta enough flexibility to optimize delivery while making sure advertising investment better reflects their commercial priorities.


And because SMART Segments continuously reevaluate product performance, prioritization can adapt as products gain or lose momentum throughout the Black Friday period.


## How should you allocate your Black Friday advertising budget?


Increasing your advertising budget doesn't automatically mean increasing your revenue or profitability.


Before scaling spend for Black Friday, examine where your existing budget is going at the product level.


A campaign might deliver a healthy overall ROAS while directing a disproportionate share of its spend toward a relatively small group of products. Some of those products may be high performers, while others may have limited profitability, declining conversion rates, or insufficient stock.


The bigger opportunity is to make your existing advertising investment work harder by improving which products receive exposure.


Focus on three principles:


- Prioritize products with stronger business potential. Look beyond historical advertising ROAS to consider revenue potential, profitability, conversion behavior, and inventory availability.
- Reduce inefficient spend. Identify products consistently consuming advertising budget without generating sufficient value, and deprioritize them where appropriate.
- Adapt as performance changes. A product performing strongly before Black Friday may lose momentum during the event, while another product may emerge as a stronger opportunity.


Remember that Meta determines delivery within its campaign optimization framework. You can influence product visibility through eligibility rules and prioritization signals, but you cannot guarantee a fixed share of campaign spend for every product group.


With Segment Prioritisation, Pattern Ad Signals helps advertisers guide Meta toward more commercially valuable products without requiring a separate budget for each segment.


The goal is to generate more value from the budget you're already investing.


## Which products should each audience see?


Meta's automation is increasingly responsible for finding relevant shoppers and determining which products they're most likely to engage with or purchase.


But while Meta understands advertising engagement and conversion behavior, it doesn't automatically have access to all the business signals that determine which products are most valuable for your company.


That's why product selection and prioritization remain essential.


Different customer groups may respond to different product strategies:


- New customers: Proven bestsellers, accessible entry-point products, and products with strong conversion potential can help introduce shoppers to your brand.
- Recent website visitors: Dynamic product recommendations can reconnect shoppers with products they've already explored, while product eligibility and prioritization strategies account for current business objectives.
- Promotion-driven shoppers: Discounted products with compelling offers, sufficient availability, and healthy margins may deserve additional visibility during Black Friday.
- Existing customers: New arrivals, complementary products, and relevant higher-value items can create opportunities for repeat purchases and increased customer value.


These are strategic considerations rather than rigid audience-to-product assignments. Meta still determines which eligible products to deliver based on its available signals and campaign settings.


The real advantage comes from combining Meta's ability to find relevant shoppers with your business's understanding of which products deserve advertising investment.


With Pattern Ad Signals, retailers can bring additional SKU-level intelligence into their catalog advertising strategy, helping Meta make better product delivery decisions that reflect both advertising performance and broader commercial objectives.


Meta knows who is likely to buy. Pattern Ad Signals helps inform which products are worth promoting.


## What creative works best for Black Friday catalog ads?


Many retailers still rely on standard product images with plain white backgrounds for their Meta catalog ads. While these images serve their purpose on product detail pages, they often do little to differentiate a brand in crowded Facebook and Instagram feeds.


During Black Friday, this becomes an even bigger challenge. Shoppers are exposed to countless promotional messages competing for their attention, making creative quality and relevance increasingly important.


But standing out is only half the challenge.


For retailers managing catalogs with thousands or even millions of SKUs, creating and maintaining relevant advertising creatives at scale is difficult. Prices change, discounts come and go, products sell out, and new promotions launch throughout the season.


Manually updating every product image, promotional badge, price, and creative variation simply isn't realistic.


### Make your product creatives stand out


Your Black Friday catalog ads should do more than display a product against a white background. They should communicate why that product is worth clicking on.


Consider incorporating:


- Promotional overlays: Highlight relevant discounts, sale prices, and limited-time offers to make your Black Friday promotions immediately recognizable.
- Lifestyle imagery: Use contextual backgrounds that help shoppers visualize products in real-life settings rather than relying exclusively on standard product packshots.
- Catalog Product Videos: Transform static product imagery into engaging video creatives, particularly suited for video-first placements such as Reels and Stories.
- Category-specific templates: Adapt creative layouts to different product categories. A beauty product, fashion item, and piece of furniture shouldn't necessarily share the same creative treatment.
- AI-powered creative enhancements: Use background removal, background generation, and virtual photoshoots to create more visually compelling product imagery without organizing individual photoshoots for every SKU.


The goal is to make products more engaging while keeping the shopping experience consistent with your brand and promotional messaging.


### Keep creatives accurate across your entire catalog


A visually attractive ad won't deliver the right experience if the price is outdated, the discount has expired, or the advertised product is no longer available.


During Black Friday, when promotions can change daily or even more frequently, maintaining creative accuracy becomes just as important as creative quality.


That's why dynamic creative templates are particularly valuable for large product catalogs.


Instead of manually producing and updating individual ads, retailers can use reusable templates that pull product information from connected catalog data, allowing supported creative elements such as prices and promotional labels to reflect updated product information.

Combined with its AI creative capabilities, Creative Factory helps brands move beyond basic product packshots and produce more relevant, visually engaging advertising assets at scale.


This makes it easier to maintain creative consistency across large catalogs, reduce repetitive production work, and respond to changing promotional priorities throughout the peak shopping season.

And producing catalog videos doesn't have to mean filming thousands of individual products.

The takeaway: during Black Friday, the challenge is making sure thousands of products have relevant, compelling, and up-to-date creatives throughout the shopping season. The retailers that can combine creative quality with scalable production and accurate product data are better positioned to make the most of their catalog advertising investment.


## What to check before Black Friday


Successful Black Friday catalog advertising starts well before the first promotion goes live. Before scaling your campaigns, make sure your product data, advertising priorities, and creatives are ready to handle rapidly changing demand.


Use this checklist in the weeks leading up to Black Friday, and review it again just before the event.


- Review SKU-level performance: Identify your strongest performers, underpromoted opportunities, and products consuming advertising spend without generating sufficient returns. Look beyond Meta's reporting by considering sales, profitability, and performance across other channels.
- Set your product priorities: Decide which products deserve greater advertising visibility and which should be deprioritized. If you're using SMART Segments and Segment Prioritisation, review your segmentation strategy and prioritization settings before the peak.
- Check inventory availability: Make sure stock information is accurate and updated frequently. Pay particular attention to popular products with limited inventory and products with incomplete size or color availability.
- Validate prices and promotions: Confirm that advertised prices and discounts match your website and catalog feed. Check that promotional start and end dates are configured correctly and expired offers are removed promptly.
- Prepare your creatives at scale: Make sure your product ads are visually engaging, reflect current promotions, and use appropriate formats for different product categories and placements. Use dynamic templates where supported to reduce manual creative updates.
- Verify tracking and catalog connections: Check that your Meta Pixel and Conversions API are functioning correctly and that the product identifiers in your events match those in your catalog.
- Finalize campaign setup: Allow sufficient time for ad reviews and campaign learning. Avoid unnecessary structural changes immediately before the event.
- Define your optimization plan: Agree on which performance indicators to monitor, when to adjust advertising priorities, and who is responsible for responding to changes in product performance, stock, and promotions.


One of the biggest Black Friday mistakes is focusing exclusively on campaign-level performance while overlooking what's happening at the product level.


A campaign can achieve its ROAS target while promoting low-margin products, missing valuable opportunities elsewhere in the catalog, or directing spend toward products with limited availability.


The key is to enter Black Friday with a clear product strategy, accurate data, and the ability to adapt as conditions change.


## What to change during Black Friday, Cyber Monday, and after


Black Friday isn't a set-it-and-forget-it event. Product demand, inventory levels, and advertising performance can shift rapidly throughout the shopping period.


### During Black Friday: Monitor performance at the SKU level


Don't rely on campaign-level ROAS alone. Look at which products are actually receiving advertising investment and whether that exposure aligns with their business potential.


Pay particular attention to:


- Product-level spend and performance: Are your strongest products receiving meaningful exposure? Are weaker-performing products consuming a disproportionate share of your budget?
- Emerging opportunities: Are there products generating strong sales on your website or through other channels that Meta hasn't promoted sufficiently?
- Inventory changes: Are products approaching stockouts while continuing to receive heavy advertising exposure?
- Creative accuracy: Are prices, promotional messages, and product availability reflected correctly in your catalog ads?


With AI-driven SMART Segments, retailers can continuously reevaluate SKU-level performance as new data becomes available. Combined with Segment Prioritisation, these insights can help advertising delivery better reflect changing product priorities without requiring constant manual campaign restructuring.


### Before Cyber Monday: Adapt to what you've learned


Black Friday performance provides valuable signals about which products and promotions resonate with shoppers.


Review which products generated the strongest returns, which categories gained momentum, and where advertising investment failed to deliver sufficient value.


Use these insights to refine product priorities ahead of Cyber Monday. Products showing strong potential may deserve greater visibility, while consistently weaker performers or products with limited inventory may need to be deprioritized.


This is also the time to refresh your creative messaging. Make sure expired Black Friday offers are removed and Cyber Monday promotions are accurately reflected across your catalog ads.


### After Cyber Monday: Follow the next wave of demand


Product priorities shouldn't remain static once Cyber Monday ends.


As shoppers move into the holiday gifting season, demand may shift toward giftable products, bundles, and items available for delivery before the holidays.


Your advertising strategy should adapt accordingly, taking into account changing demand, inventory availability, delivery deadlines, and promotional opportunities.


After the holiday season, priorities may shift again toward excess inventory, seasonal clearance, or products relevant to New Year shopping.


The objective remains the same throughout: continuously identify which products have the greatest business potential and align your advertising investment with those opportunities.

## Frequently asked questions


### When should I start Black Friday Facebook ads?


Plan for the whole of November, with Black Friday as its peak. Ideally, your campaigns, product priorities, promotional data, and creatives should be prepared and tested before November begins, so you can adjust through the month instead of rebuilding.


Meta typically reviews ads within 24 hours, although reviews can take longer. New ad sets may also need time to complete their learning phase, depending on the volume of optimization events they generate.


Launching early gives you time to resolve potential issues and avoid making major campaign changes during the most important shopping days.


### Should I use catalog ads for Black Friday?


Yes. Meta catalog ads are particularly valuable for retailers managing large product assortments because they allow advertisers to dynamically promote relevant products based on available catalog data and Meta's delivery signals.


However, having a large catalog doesn't automatically mean your advertising budget will be distributed toward the products most valuable to your business.


Combining catalog ads with SKU-level performance insights and product prioritization helps align advertising exposure with broader business goals, including profitability, revenue potential, and inventory priorities.


### How do I stop Facebook ads from promoting products that are running out?


Start by keeping inventory data accurate and updating your catalog feed frequently, particularly during high-demand periods.


Meta doesn't show out-of-stock items in catalog ads at all, but products with low remaining stock can still be promoted while they're listed as available.


To manage this risk, monitor inventory alongside advertising performance and adjust product eligibility or prioritization when needed.


Pattern Ad Signals helps retailers incorporate relevant product and business data into their segmentation strategies, allowing stock-related priorities to be considered alongside advertising performance.


### What creative works best for Black Friday on Facebook?


Effective Black Friday catalog creatives should make products stand out while communicating relevant offers clearly.


Rather than relying exclusively on standard product images with white backgrounds, retailers can use promotional overlays, category-specific templates, lifestyle imagery, and Catalog Product Videos to create more engaging ads.


For large catalogs, scalability is equally important. Dynamic creative templates can help retailers maintain consistent branding and keep supported product information and promotions up to date without manually redesigning thousands of individual ads.


With Pattern Ad Signals' Creative Factory, retailers can create and manage catalog creatives at scale, combining image and video templates with AI-powered creative capabilities to make more products stand out during peak shopping periods.
